questions.question: Which mechanism is primarily utilized by the operating system to prevent thrashing?
questions.title: Preventing thrashing
options: process must request and be allocated all the resources…
Working Set Model
external fragmentation
During a context switch, the OS saves the current…
questions.answer: Working Set Model

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Thrashing happens when the system spends more time paging (swapping) than executing, because too many processes compete for too little physical memory.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The **Working Set Model** (and the related Page Fault Frequency approach) is primarily used — it tracks the set of pages a process actively needs and ensures each process is allocated enough frames to hold its working set, preventing excessive page faulting.

questions.question: Which critical piece of information is NOT typically stored within a Process Control Block?
questions.title: NOT stored in a Process Control Block (PCB)
options: blocks the entire process (all its threads)
the actual user program code/data segment contents (the…
60ms
An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…
questions.answer: the actual user program code/data segment contents (the…

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: A PCB stores process state, program counter, CPU registers, CPU scheduling info, memory management info, accounting info, and I/O status info.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Data such as **the actual user program code/data segment contents (the process's full memory contents)** is NOT stored in the PCB itself — the PCB stores pointers/metadata about memory, not the memory contents.

questions.question: Peterson's solution is a classic software-based synchronization algorithm restricted to:
questions.title: Peterson's Solution — restriction
options: exactly two processes
reduced memory usage
Working Set Model
questions.answer: exactly two processes

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Peterson's solution is restricted to providing mutual exclusion for **exactly two processes** and requires strict alternation support with shared variables (`turn` and `flag[]`); it doesn't scale to more processes and assumes a simple memory model without instruction reordering.

questions.question: When a child process terminates but its parent has not yet called wait(), what type of process does the child become?
questions.title: Child terminates before parent calls wait()
options: zombie process
smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer…
Low-level formatting establishes the physical structure of…
11 bits
questions.answer: zombie process

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The child becomes a **zombie process** — it has finished execution, but its exit status/PCB entry remains in the process table until the parent reads it via `wait()`.

questions.question: Which of the following strict priority scheduling scenarios unequivocally leads to the phenomenon known as priority inversion in a real-time operating system?
questions.title: Scenario causing priority inversion
options: An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…
VFS provides an abstraction layer that lets the OS…
Priority inversion occurs when a high-priority task is blocked…
questions.answer: Priority inversion occurs when a high-priority task is blocked…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Priority inversion occurs when a **high-priority task is blocked waiting for a resource held by a low-priority task, while a medium-priority task (not needing that resource) preempts the low-priority task and runs instead** — effectively letting a medium-priority task delay a high-priority one indirectly.

questions.question: What is the fundamental operational advantage of an inverted page table when directly compared to a traditional hierarchical page table in modern operating systems?
questions.title: Inverted page table — advantage
options: 11 bits
reduced memory usage
external fragmentation
questions.answer: reduced memory usage

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: An inverted page table's key advantage is **reduced memory usage** — it maintains only one entry per physical frame (not per virtual page per process), so table size scales with the amount of physical memory rather than growing with each process's virtual address space.

questions.question: During the system boot sequence, what is the primary role of the Master Boot Record (MBR)?
questions.title: Master Boot Record (MBR) — role
options: process must request and be allocated all the resources…
external fragmentation
store the partition table and a small bootloader/boot code
An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…
questions.answer: store the partition table and a small bootloader/boot code

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The MBR's primary role is to **store the partition table and a small bootloader/boot code** that the BIOS loads and executes first, which then locates and loads the operating system's actual boot loader from the active partition.

questions.question: What is established during the 'physical formatting' or 'low-level formatting' of a disk?
questions.title: Physical (low-level) formatting establishes
options: Low-level formatting establishes the physical structure of…
accesses a page that is part of its logical…
An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…
smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer…
questions.answer: Low-level formatting establishes the physical structure of…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Low-level formatting establishes the **physical structure of the disk — sectors, tracks, and cylinders — writing the addressing markers the controller uses to locate data**, preparing the raw disk surface before a file system can be created on it.

questions.question: What specifically triggers a hardware trap known as a 'page fault' during execution?
questions.title: What triggers a page fault
options: exactly two processes
Working Set Model
accesses a page that is part of its logical…
zombie process
questions.answer: accesses a page that is part of its logical…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: A page fault is triggered when a process **accesses a page that is part of its logical address space but is not currently present in physical memory (RAM)** — the MMU detects the missing valid mapping and traps to the OS to load the page from disk.

questions.question: In a multi-threaded process executing on an architecture featuring a strict Many-to-One thread mapping model, what occurs when a single user-level thread invokes a blocking system call?
questions.title: Many-to-One thread model — blocking system call
options: smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer…
Low-level formatting establishes the physical structure of…
the actual user program code/data segment contents (the…
blocks the entire process (all its threads)
questions.answer: blocks the entire process (all its threads)

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Because all user-level threads map to a single kernel thread, a blocking system call from one thread **blocks the entire process (all its threads)**, since the kernel is unaware of the individual user-level threads and only sees one kernel-level entity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Virtual File System (VFS) layer in an operating system?
questions.title: Purpose of the Virtual File System (VFS)
options: 11 bits
VFS provides an abstraction layer that lets the OS…
accesses a page that is part of its logical…
questions.answer: VFS provides an abstraction layer that lets the OS…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: VFS provides an **abstraction layer that lets the OS support multiple different file system types (ext4, NTFS, FAT, NFS, etc.) through a single, uniform interface**, so applications can access files without needing to know the underlying file system's specific implementation.

questions.question: Which of the following hardware devices is classically categorized as a block device?
questions.title: Classic block device
options: Working Set Model
hard disk drive (HDD/SSD)
60ms
questions.answer: hard disk drive (HDD/SSD)

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: A **hard disk drive (HDD/SSD)** is the classic block device — it transfers data in fixed-size blocks and supports random access (as opposed to character devices like keyboards/mice, which transfer data as a stream, one character at a time).

questions.question: What is a primary purpose of buffering in I/O systems?
questions.title: Purpose of I/O buffering
options: An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…
smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer…
blocks the entire process (all its threads)
the actual user program code/data segment contents (the…
questions.answer: smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Buffering's primary purpose is to **smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer (like the CPU) and a slower I/O device**, allowing overlapped/asynchronous data transfer instead of forcing the CPU to wait on slow I/O, and reducing the number of actual I/O operations.

questions.question: Which of the following file allocation methods suffers from the problem of external fragmentation?
questions.title: File allocation method suffering from external fragmentation
options: Contiguous allocation
During a context switch, the OS saves the current…
Low-level formatting establishes the physical structure of…
11 bits
questions.answer: Contiguous allocation

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Contiguous allocation** suffers from external fragmentation, since files must occupy contiguous blocks and repeated allocation/deallocation leaves scattered free gaps too small individually to satisfy new requests (Linked and Indexed allocation avoid this since blocks needn't be contiguous).

questions.question: A system uses 32-bit logical addresses, an 8KB page size, and 4-byte page table entries. If the system utilizes a two-level hierarchical paging scheme where the outer page table fits exactly in one single page, how many bits are allocated to the outer page table index?
questions.title: Two-level paging — outer page table index bits
options: 13 bits
7 bits
11 bits
10 bits
questions.answer: 11 bits

sections.label: Given
sections.content: 32-bit logical address, page size = 8KB = 2¹³ → offset = 13 bits. Outer table fits in exactly one page (8KB), and each PTE = 4 bytes.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. Remaining bits after offset = 32 − 13 = 19 bits (shared between outer index + inner index).
2. Number of entries the outer table can hold = page size ÷ entry size = 8KB ÷ 4B = 2¹³ ÷ 2² = 2¹¹ entries.
3. So the outer index needs **11 bits** to address those 2¹¹ entries.
4. (Inner index then takes the remaining 19 − 11 = 8 bits.)

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 11 bits.

questions.question: What happens during a context switch?
questions.title: What happens during a context switch
options: During a context switch, the OS saves the current…
11 bits
hard disk drive (HDD/SSD)
questions.answer: During a context switch, the OS saves the current…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: During a context switch, the OS **saves the current process's state (CPU registers, program counter, PCB info) into its PCB, then loads the saved state of the next process to run from its PCB into the CPU registers** — this is pure overhead (no useful process work is done during the switch itself).

questions.question: Consider a standard counting semaphore initialized to 5. Three concurrent processes A, B, and C each execute an asynchronous loop containing wait() and signal() operations. If the ultimate sequence of operations executed across all processes is exactly 6 wait() calls and 4 signal() calls, what is the final numeric value of the semaphore?
questions.title: Counting semaphore — final value

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Initial value = 5, total wait() calls = 6, total signal() calls = 4.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Each `wait()` decrements the semaphore by 1; each `signal()` increments it by 1. Regardless of interleaving order (once all operations have completed), the net effect is additive: Final = Initial − (waits) + (signals).
**Calculation:** 5 − 6 + 4 = **3**.

questions.question: Consider a system using Round Robin scheduling with a time quantum of 20ms and a context switch overhead of 5ms. If a single process requires exactly 50ms of CPU time to complete, what is the total time it occupies the CPU including the necessary context switches before it terminates?
questions.title: Round Robin — total CPU occupation time
options: 56ms
60ms
59ms
61ms
questions.answer: 60ms

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Time quantum = 20ms, context switch overhead = 5ms, total burst needed = 50ms, single process only.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. 1st quantum: runs 20ms → 30ms remaining → context switch (5ms).
2. 2nd quantum: runs 20ms → 10ms remaining → context switch (5ms).
3. 3rd quantum: runs remaining 10ms → process finishes (no further context switch needed since nothing else to switch to).
4. Total = 20 + 5 + 20 + 5 + 10 = **60ms**.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 60ms.

questions.question: Which specific memory fragmentation issue is the Buddy System allocator primarily engineered to minimize, and what corresponding structural compromise does it inherently introduce?
questions.title: Buddy System — fragmentation minimized & compromise
options: blocks the entire process (all its threads)
external fragmentation
the actual user program code/data segment contents (the…
questions.answer: external fragmentation

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The Buddy System is engineered to minimize **external fragmentation** (blocks are split/merged as power-of-2 sized "buddies," making coalescing of adjacent free blocks fast and simple). The structural compromise it introduces is **increased internal fragmentation**, since allocations are rounded up to the nearest power of 2, wasting space within the allocated block.

questions.question: A UNIX file system uses inodes with 12 direct pointers, one singly indirect pointer, one doubly indirect pointer, and one triply indirect pointer. If the block size is 4KB and a pointer requires 4 bytes, what is the maximum file size supported using exclusively the direct and singly indirect pointers?
questions.title: UNIX inode — max file size using direct + singly indirect only

sections.label: Given
sections.content: 12 direct pointers, block size = 4KB, pointer size = 4 bytes.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. Direct blocks: 12 × 4KB = 48 KB.
2. Pointers per indirect block = block size ÷ pointer size = 4KB ÷ 4B = 1024 pointers.
3. Singly indirect capacity = 1024 × 4KB = 4096 KB (4 MB).
4. Total = 48 KB + 4096 KB = **4144 KB (≈ 4.05 MB)**.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the functional limitation of an ordinary Unix pipe?
questions.title: Functional limitation of an ordinary UNIX pipe
options: Working Set Model
VFS provides an abstraction layer that lets the OS…
An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…
questions.answer: An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports only one-way…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: An ordinary (unnamed) UNIX pipe supports **only one-way (unidirectional) communication between related processes (typically parent-child, sharing a common ancestor)** — it cannot be used for communication between unrelated processes, unlike named pipes (FIFOs).

questions.question: In deadlock prevention protocols, the 'Hold and Wait' condition can be explicitly eliminated by successfully enforcing which of the following strict system resource allocation methods?
questions.title: Eliminating 'Hold and Wait' in deadlock prevention
options: Low-level formatting establishes the physical structure of…
11 bits
process must request and be allocated all the resources…
smooth out speed mismatches between a fast producer/consumer…
questions.answer: process must request and be allocated all the resources…

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Hold and Wait can be eliminated by enforcing that a **process must request and be allocated all the resources it will ever need at once, before it starts execution** (or alternatively, a process must release all currently held resources before requesting any new ones) — ensuring a process never holds one resource while waiting for another.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a process and a thread?
questions.title: What is the key difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads within a process share the same memory/address space; processes have separate ones
Processes always run faster than threads
A thread can exist without belonging to a process
Threads cannot communicate with each other
questions.answer: Threads within a process share the same memory/address space; processes have separate ones

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: A process is an independent execution unit with its own memory space; threads are lightweight execution units within a process.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Multiple threads within the same process share the same address space (code, data, heap) and can communicate directly through shared memory, while separate processes have completely isolated memory spaces** and must use IPC mechanisms (pipes, sockets, shared memory) to communicate.

questions.question: What is a race condition?
questions.title: What is a race condition?
options: An outcome that depends unpredictably on the relative timing of concurrent operations
A process that runs faster than expected
A deadlock caused by circular resource waiting
A scheduling algorithm favoring shorter jobs
questions.answer: An outcome that depends unpredictably on the relative timing of concurrent operations

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Race conditions occur when multiple threads/processes access shared data concurrently without proper synchronization.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **A race condition occurs when the correctness of a program's outcome depends on the unpredictable relative timing/interleaving of multiple threads or processes accessing shared data** — typically fixed using synchronization primitives like mutexes or semaphores to enforce mutual exclusion.

questions.question: What is the difference between internal and external fragmentation?
questions.title: What is the difference between internal and external fragmen
options: Internal fragmentation wastes space within an allocated block; external is scattered free space between blocks
Internal fragmentation only happens in paging; external only in segmentation
External fragmentation means data is corrupted; internal means it is lost
Both terms mean exactly the same thing
questions.answer: Internal fragmentation wastes space within an allocated block; external is scattered free space between blocks

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Both are memory-management inefficiencies but occur differently.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Internal fragmentation is wasted space WITHIN an allocated fixed-size block** (e.g., a process needing 18KB allocated a 20KB page, wasting 2KB inside it), **while external fragmentation is wasted space BETWEEN allocated blocks** — free memory scattered in small, non-contiguous chunks too small individually to satisfy new requests.
